relevance_note: The paper reports an in-scope person with HA20 and a TNFAIP3 variant: "Whole-exome sequencing revealed a novel c.1467_1468delinsAT heterozygous mutation in the gene TNFAIP3".
method_note: Read the three supplied files only; no script was used to transcribe tables, every cell was copied by hand and re-checked against the Markdown. Table 2 is a patients-as-columns table (headers P1, P2, P3, P4, P5), so its rows were read as label-to-cell segments and its own 'Reference' row was copied into source_reference_in_review for each patient (P1=[13], P2=[14], P3=[14], P4=[15], P5=This study). The case-report patient has no own label in the text ('the patient', 'our patient' are role words), but Table 2 column 5 has label P5, Reference 'This study' and the same variant as the patient, so I used P5 and treated the text as describing P5. His parents and his sister, tested negative, are in scope as relatives; the paper states no sex for them, so they are 'parent of P5', 'parent of P5 2' and 'sister of P5'. Contradictions found: (1) Table 2 gives Arthralgia 'yes' for P2 and P5 while the Discussion says 'these five patients did not present with other clinical manifestations of HA20, including early onset IBD, muscle-skeletal disorders with arthralgia and arthritis, and recurrent fever'; both rows were emitted in phenotypic_features and the checklist items left 'not reported'. (2) The protein change is printed as 'p.Q490*' in the text but '(p.Glu490*)' in the Figure 1 legend. (3) The abstract says oral ulcers began 'since early childhood' while Table 2 gives age at the appearance of initial symptoms 5 for P5; I recorded the age from Table 2. No cell in this paper uses the ' / ' stacked-value separator; Table 1 has repeated header cells and empty cells, and empty cells were treated as not reported. Table 2 'NM' is defined as 'not mentioned' in the table notes and was always treated as not reported; 'no' in that table is taken as a stated absence of the diseases listed for P1 in the 'Other autoinflammatory diseases' row (cytopaenias, enteropathy and interstitial lung disease). Text statements of normal or negative findings ('normal lipid profile', 'normal thyroid function', 'vision and hearing were normal') were recorded per D-27 as the abnormality they rule out. The only Table 1 cells used for an absence are the two rows whose own 'Normal values' column defines the value as normal (CRP 5.8 mg/L against 0–6, and 'Urine ketone' marked '(-)'); all other Table 1 numbers were read as reported values only. The checklist row 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation' is 'observed' for P1 (enteropathy), 'excluded' for P5 and 'not reported' for P2-P4 (the row lists those diseases only for P1), while 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' and 'interstitial lung disease' are 'observed' for P1 and 'excluded' for P3, P4 and P5, and the composite item 'arthritis or arthralgia' is left 'not reported' wherever the table and the group sentence disagree. Variant fields were filled from a person's own table cell or from a sentence naming that person, so variant_type is only recorded for P5 ('stop-gained type mutation') and not for P1-P4 from the general list 'nonsense or frameshift variants'; zygosity is only recorded for P5, because the sentence 'a c.1467_1468delinsAT heterozygous mutation in the gene TNFAIP3' names the patient, not his variant-carrying relatives. The checklist item 'type 1 diabetes' is 'observed' for P3 and P4 with evidence_basis 'inferred from group statement', because their own 'Age at the onset of diabetes' cells are 'NM' while the paper states these are cases of 'HA20 in combination with T1DM'. The paper's statement 'The patient's parents and sister were found to be devoid of this variant' makes the patient's variant not inherited from either tested parent; inheritance was nevertheless left 'not reported' because the paper gives no family member carrying the variant (D-24).
